vehicle.gvwr: Class 1: 6,000 lb or less (2,722 kg or less)

pids.0156: long term secondary O2 trim bank 1 (%)

signals.name: odometer
signals.verified: read against the dashboard one minute into a running log (142,934 mi), and again as +5 km over a 17-minute drive

signals.name: coolant temperature (SAE scale)
signals.verified: raw - 40, the SAE form. Against the legislated coolant PID: r=0.999, slope 0.979, offset +3.4 degC -- a DIFFERENT measuring point on the engine rather than a mirror of 0105, which is what the offset shows. Recorded as inferred only because the sample count behind the r was not preserved; the correlation itself is well above the 0.90 floor.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of the enhanced blocks

signals.name: oil temperature
signals.verified: value x 0.75 - 48, the community temperature form. Anchored against the legislated coolant PID rather than assumed, at r=0.9896 with zero lag. That establishes it is an engine temperature; that it is specifically the OIL temperature rests on the block it sits in and on 0x2244 reading as a temperature range throughout. Not swept at all until 2026-08-23.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of 0x2258xx

signals.name: reference torque
signals.verified: raw x 0.1 gives 398.9 Nm, the stock N55 reference figure, which is the external check. NOT a constant: it moved between 3985 and 3989 counts within one drive, so it is a live baseline rather than a calibration value. 2258BA is expressed as a percentage of it, and horsepower as 2258BA x 224517 x rpm. Same tuning caveat as 2258BA: the convention transfers, the number may not.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of 0x2258xx

signals.name: rev limiter
signals.verified: Constant 6800. Confirmed because a wide-open-throttle pull reached exactly 6800 rpm -- the value the field holds is the value the engine stopped at, which is an external anchor rather than a correlation. Note the 7000 in the gauge profile's RPM row is the dial's full scale, not the limiter.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of the enhanced blocks

signals.name: engine load
signals.verified: raw / 2.55, giving percent. Slope 0.976 against the legislated load PID. Recorded as inferred because the r and sample count were not preserved.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of the enhanced blocks

signals.name: oil pressure
signals.verified: 16-bit big-endian, byte 0 on the 7DF broadcast. SCALE IS UNVERIFIED and the alarms built on it are off for that reason. Absolute, not gauge: it reads 03E8-0410 with the engine stopped, which is 1000-1040 mbar, atmospheric -- and skipping the barometric subtraction is what made an earlier decode read about 15 psi high, one atmosphere. Firming this up needs a known-pressure anchor, the way oil temperature was anchored against the coolant PID.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of 0x2258xx

signals.name: crank torque
signals.verified: Anchored on engine behaviour, three ways independent of scale: it collapses to zero on overrun, it peaks at 5940 rpm for power and 3800 rpm for torque -- the N55's published curve -- and it correlates r=+0.938 against MAF-derived power. Scale then pinned at 0.1 Nm/count from the DME's own calibration convention. Reported live as a percentage of 224517. The donor car is TUNED, so the magnitudes here are this vehicle's rather than a stock N55's; the 0.1 Nm/count convention is what transfers, and it should hold on any MEVD17.2.
signals.source: identified in this project's own sweeping of 0x2258xx. UNNAMED IN ALL SIX COMMUNITY BMW LISTS -- this is not a decode anyone published, it was worked out from the car.

source: obd-discover, 4 on-car capture(s) 2026-08; Mode-01 support scanned 2026-08-29
notes: 535i (F10). 2258xx and 224Axx are absent from the community list entirely. Enhanced Mode-22 reads in the 58xx block on the 7DF functional broadcast decode byte 0 only; a full u16 read there ingests NAK frames. That constraint comes from obd-gauge-cluster's profile and matters for anyone decoding 2258xx from a broadcast. 225817 and 2258EB were oil-temperature candidates in the 58xx block and are byte-identical to each other on 99.51% of 1,427 logged rows -- one signal under two identifiers, which is what makes them candidates rather than two findings. Horsepower on the dash is computed from 2258BA x 224517 x rpm; everything else shown there is standard Mode-01, not enhanced DIDs. OPEN: 2258F3 also reads 0x1A90 (6800) as a constant in this project's own drive logs, the same value as the rev limiter at 224A2E. Whether it is a mirror of the limiter, a second limit, or a coincidence is untested.
